answers.a: The Manila International Research Conference 2026 (MIRC 2026) is a hybrid international academic conference that brings together researchers, academicians, practitioners, policymakers and students from diverse disciplines. It focuses on the role of artificial intelligence, sustainability and innovation in building resilient, inclusive and future‑ready communities. The main conference takes place on 29‑30 September 2026 at the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) in Intramuros, Manila.

The conference runs from 27 to 30 September 2026.  
- 27 Sept 2026: Hospitality & Tourism sub‑conference at DLSU‑CSB.  
- 29–30 Sept 2026: Main conference at Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM).
The conference takes place at Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM), located at Gen. Luna Cor. Muralla Streets, Intramuros, Manila, Philippines 1002.

answers.q: How do I get to PLM from the LRT?
answers.a: From the Central Terminal (LRT‑1) you’ll exit the station and walk about 860 m to the PLM campus – roughly an 11‑minute walk. The station is the nearest LRT stop to the university.

answers.a: Registration opens at 7:00 AM on 29 September 2026 (the first day of the main conference) in the GEE Lobby.

The conference has four tracks:
- BGL – Business, Government, Law  
- EASS – Education, Arts, Social Science, Social Work  
- HS – Health Sciences  
- STEA – Science, Technology, Engineering, Architecture
STEA stands for Science, Technology, Engineering, Architecture. It’s one of the four conference tracks.
BGL is the code for the Business, Government, Law track.
HS stands for Health Sciences, one of the four conference tracks.
EASS stands for Education, Arts, Social Science, Social Work.

answers.q: Where is the Justo Albert Auditorium?

- Dexter Pizza – Sisay’s – Budget Eats & Carinderias, budget — under ₱200 per person (price is an indicative estimate). Pizza and Filipino fare on Cabildo Street, about 7 min walk (560 m).  
- Flower Stories Café – Cafés & Coffee, moderate — ₱200–₱500 per person (price is an indicative estimate). Small café on Magallanes Street, about 7 min walk (540 m).  
- J’s Cuisine – Restaurants & Heritage Dining, moderate — ₱200–₱500 per person (price is an indicative estimate). Filipino restaurant on Anda Street, about 9 min walk (700 m).

answers.q: What can I see in Intramuros?
answers.a:
You can visit these Intramuros highlights, all within a short walk from the PLM venue:
- Memorare — Manila 1945 (Anda Street · Plazuela de Santa Isabel, free, ~10 min visit, 6 min walk)
- Museo de Intramuros (Arzobispo corner Anda Street · Reconstructed San Ignacio Church, ₱200 (₱160 students/seniors/PWD), ~1 hr, 6 min walk)
- Plaza México (Aduana Street, free, ~15 min, 11 min walk)
- Plazuela de Santa Isabel (Anda corner Real Street, free, ~10 min, 6 min walk)
- San Agustin Church (General Luna Street · Opposite Plaza San Luis, free, ~30 min, 3 min walk)
- Santa Lucia Barracks Ruins (Santa Lucia Street, free, ~15 min, 3 min walk)

answers.q: Where can I stay inside the walls?
answers.a:
You can stay at these boutique hotels inside Intramuros:

The Bayleaf Intramuros – ₱2,800 – ₱13,300 per night (≈₱2,765 for a Superior; suites up to ₱13,000). Located at Muralla corner Victoria Street, on the eastern wall beside Lyceum of the Philippines University, about a 5‑minute walk (430 m) from the PLM venue. It is the only full‑service boutique hotel inside the walls and also houses the Cioccolata café.

White Knight Hotel Intramuros – ₱1,750 – ₱5,100 per night (≈₱2,000 typical). Situated in the Plaza San Luis Complex on General Luna Street, opposite San Agustin Church, about a 4‑minute walk (310 m) from the venue. Housed in a restored Spanish colonial mansion, it offers 29 rooms and an in‑house café.
